# Motion production protocol

Version: 0.2.1. Applies to the production of motions and supporting packages. This protocol supplies workflow instructions, not substantive law or an automated legal determination.

## Production contract

Every drafting assignment identifies one existing motion ID, exact output folder, responsible drafting role, requested relief, jurisdiction, procedural posture, applicable burden, current source inputs, and next concrete artifact. The responsible drafting role remains accountable for completing the motion when specialists supply supporting work. An assignment to draft ends with a substantive draft, not only an issue list, research summary, or folder scaffold.

Maintain separate milestones: analysis available; draft written; supporting package assembled; substantive review completed; counsel authorized for filing. A tracker task marked done does not establish any other milestone. Status changes must name the artifact version and reviewed scope. Do not replace an existing tracker with a parallel status ledger.

## Sequence and outputs

1. **Define relief.** State the action requested from the court, its legal basis, and the narrower alternative. Identify the evidence, statement, proceeding, or deadline affected. Separate distinct remedies rather than combining them because they concern the same actor.
2. **Map the issue.** Use an issue tree to separate threshold procedure, elements, burdens, supporting facts, opposing arguments, prejudice or materiality, remedy, and preservation. Shared evidence may support multiple issues; cross-reference it rather than forcing artificial exclusivity.
3. **Build a compact proof map.** For every necessary proposition, identify source ID, pinpoint or time range, exact proposition supported, contrary material, evidentiary status, and any missing link. A summary is a navigation aid, not a substitute for its underlying source. Record possession, authentication, and substantive support separately.
4. **Verify the law.** Record the precise proposition, governing jurisdiction, authority level, quotation/pinpoint, current verification method/date, adverse authority, and procedural fit. Distinguish textual verification from subsequent-treatment research. Do not claim a licensed citator check without the supporting check record.
5. **Write the motion.** Use IRAC/CREAC to develop the application in clear third-person professional prose. Explain how particular supported facts satisfy each requirement. Keep framework names, model instructions, internal review dialogue, and strategic scoring out of the court-facing paper.
6. **Draft the order alongside the prayer.** Match each requested action to an operative paragraph: responsible person or entity, defined items, permissible deadline or trigger, protection/access terms, reporting obligation, and hearing or compliance mechanism. Do not fabricate a court date or imply that an unsigned order has been entered.
7. **Test the argument.** Use the argument worksheet to state the strongest opposing position and the source-supported response. Reconstruct the opposing case fairly. Identify unsupported causal jumps and distinguish error, contradiction, knowledge, intent, prejudice, and remedy.
8. **Assemble the package.** Add supporting memorandum when useful or required, exhibit index with source references, any required affidavit/proffer draft, proposed order, service preparation, hearing outline, and preservation notes. Do not invent signatures, sworn personal knowledge, exhibits, or completed service.
9. **Review and hand off.** Deliver exact file paths, version/hash, substantive changes, unresolved issues, scope reviewed, and next action. A defect list must identify a passage and proposed repair rather than merely saying that review is required.

## Continue drafting when a limited input is unavailable

Use verified material to complete the portions that can responsibly be written. Identify a necessary unresolved predicate in the internal worksheet and, where appropriate, a clearly labeled draft placeholder or proffer. Do not invent facts to fill it. Missing requested discovery can be the subject of a production request; it is not automatically an obstacle to drafting that request. Do not imply that an unproduced item exists without a stated basis.

Respect closed-search instructions. Reopen a local search only upon new information or changed authorization. Distinguish a closed local search from possible external acquisition. Do not repeat a request for information already supplied and recorded at the applicable scope.

## Minimum motion package

| Artifact | Required substance |
|---|---|
| Motion | Caption, posture, precise relief, supported facts, legal standard, developed application, opposing position/response, prayer, signature/service preparation as applicable |
| Proposed order | Executable provisions corresponding to the prayer; findings/conclusions where appropriate |
| Argument worksheet | Elements/burden; claim, grounds, warrant, backing, qualifier, rebuttal and response; causal links and alternative explanations |
| Source and authority maps | Traceable source locations, pinpoints, adverse material, law verification and remaining limitations |
| Hearing and preservation notes | Exhibits/witnesses, factual disputes for resolution, anticipated questions, requested rulings, objections and record-making tasks |
| Review handoff | Actual artifact paths, version, review findings, unresolved decisions, responsible role, next action |

The package may use existing lifecycle folders and combine small supporting documents. No new taxonomy or redundant source copies are required.

## Release boundaries

Drafting is distinct from filing. A source gap or unresolved authority affects the relevant proposition or requested remedy, not every unrelated workstream. The package must not be labeled filing-ready until its applicable record, authority, procedure, service, preservation, and counsel decisions are complete. An automated validator can identify inconsistency; it cannot adjudicate credibility, establish scientific feasibility, or supply attorney approval.

## Portable integration

The Controller routes drafting to motion-brief-drafting, evidence questions to evidence-matrix-admissibility, authority questions to legal-research-verification, and hearing/preservation work to their existing specialist roles. These are responsibility assignments; this document does not itself launch agents or authorize new services. Existing matter operating rules govern retrieval, confidentiality, and source registration.
